title: Get live prompts on screen during calls from your notes
summary: A marketer built a Mac app with Claude Code that listens to calls, shows question and number cards from his wiki, then writes summaries and draft follow-ups.
agent_role: Claude Code built the app. The app listens to calls, surfaces relevant cards from the author's wiki, and drafts summaries, action items and follow-up emails for the author to use.
outcome: Author says it feels like a co-pilot on every call, but he is still working out how to keep it from being distracting.
what_they_did: The author used Claude Code to build a Mac app that listens to his calls. No bot joins the meeting. The app is linked to his personal wiki of brands, clients and playbooks. When someone raises a topic, it shows cards with questions to ask or numbers to quote. After the call it writes a summary, a list of actions and a draft follow-up.
how_it_went: He says it is like having a co-pilot on every call.
worth_knowing: He is still figuring out how to use the on-screen cards without being distracted by them.
prompt: Help me build a small Mac app that listens to my computer's audio during calls. Connect it to my notes folder at [notes folder path], which covers [my clients and playbooks]. While I talk, show short cards on screen with key questions or numbers when a matching topic comes up. After the call, write a summary, a list of actions and a draft follow-up email for me to review. Do not send anything automatically. Show me your plan before writing code.

curation.rationale: An original call assistant built with Claude Code that pulls from a personal wiki and drafts follow-ups. It is only a short author's account with no demo or numbers.
